reproduction_target: A STAR-Protocols-style methods/protocol paper (companion to Adami et al., Cell Genomics 2025) describing an end-to-end framework for CRISPRi silencing of evolutionarily young full-length LINE-1 (L1HS/L1PA) retrotransposons in human iPSCs, plus the on-/off-target validation analyses. Computational target: (1) retrieval of a TE-subfamily consensus sequence from Dfam; (2) gRNA design against that consensus with CRISPick (GRCh38, CRISPRi, SpyoCas9) or manual PAM-adjacent design; (3) in-silico target prediction by command-line BLAT with a verbatim example command (-stepSize=1 -repMatch=2000 -minScore=15) and a UCSC-BLAT single-locus specificity check; (4) annotation of BLAT hits by bedtools intersect against RepeatMasker, exon and intron annotations, with a verbatim example command; (5) post-filtering of BLAT false positives by alignment-length/mismatch/PAM criteria; (6) unique-mapping bulk RNA-seq analysis with STAR 2.7.8a (--outFilterMultimapNmax 1, --outFilterMismatchNoverLmax 0.03, --sjdbGTFfile GENCODE); (7) strand-specific bigwig/heatmap profiling with deepTools 2.4.5 (bamCoverage, computeMatrix, plotHeatmap); (8) strand splitting by SAM flag with samtools 1.16.1 followed by count matrices over young L1 elements; (9) custom GTF entries covering 500 bp upstream of the L1 TSS in the opposite direction to capture L1-ORF0 transcription; (10) HOMER 5.1 peak calling on dCas9, H3K4me3 and H3K9me3 CUT&RUN data; (11) bedtools annotation of those peaks. Wet-lab steps (hiPSC culture, gRNA cloning into Addgene_71237, third-generation lentiviral production and titration, MOI-10 transduction and GFP+ FACS selection, native and cross-linked CUT&RUN bench work, ORF1p western blot / immunocytochemistry) are W, out of scope for computational reproduction.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis list built from the bioRxiv v1 JATS source XML (curl with browser user-agent into an isolated per-paper scratch directory /tmp/stage1_10.1101_2025.10.24.684366/; 82,455 bytes; the title phrase 'CRISPRi-mediated silencing of retrotransposons' was confirmed present in the fetched XML, so this is the correct paper and not another assessor's fetch). IMPORTANT ROUTING CAVEAT: this is a PROTOCOL paper, and its own availability statement says verbatim 'No original data or code was generated in this publication. All the data or code presented in this work have been published in the original research paper Adami et al., 2025.' The GEO accession and the two DOI-versioned GitHub/Zenodo code deposits it cites therefore belong to the companion research article; the protocol paper links them but does not itself generate them. Two boundary calls follow from this and should be re-checked by the orchestrator. (a) CODE AXIS: steps C7-C12, which correspond to the bulk-RNA-seq and CUT&RUN pipelines, were scored code=2 because the linked, live, DOI-archived repository Molecular-Neurogenetics/L1CRISPR_Adami_2025 names 'Snakefile_bulkRNAseq' and 'Snakefile_cutnrun' plus their config/samplesheet JSONs directly in its README prose - i.e. an exact deposited implementation of those steps plausibly exists. The gRNA-design/BLAT steps C1-C6 have no counterpart in that repository README and were scored code=1 (reconstructable from prose only; the BLAT and bedtools example commands are given verbatim in the protocol text but live nowhere executable). (b) CAPTURE CLAIM: scored 'release_snapshot' because the paper cites two Zenodo-DOI-versioned code archives (10.5281/zenodo.14362613 for trusTEr, 10.5281/zenodo.15638389 for L1CRISPR_Adami_2025) plus two further Zenodo data/resource deposits. Under the protocol v0.2.6 gate that makes stage2_candidate=true. The competing reading is 'exact_pins_partial' (four tools carry exact versions in prose - STAR 2.7.8a, deepTools 2.4.5, samtools 1.16.1, HOMER 5.1 - while BLAT, bedtools, CRISPick and Dfam carry none, and the repository README contains no environment/install/conda/container section at all); that reading would set stage2_candidate=false. release_snapshot was chosen because it is the strictly higher claim on the enum ladder and because a DOI-pinned Snakemake repository is exactly the artifact class a Stage-2 code check can convert into R-star. Version axis is capped at 1 throughout per the Stage-1 rule, and the top verdict is RI. Wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: Retrieve the TE-subfamily consensus sequence as FASTA from the Dfam database (https://www.dfam.org/home); in the case study, a 5' UTR consensus obtained from an alignment of human-specific L1HS and hominoid-specific L1PA2 5' UTRs - no Dfam release version, no Dfam family accession (DF number), and no alignment tool or settings for the L1HS/L1PA2 consensus merge

gRNA design against the consensus with CRISPick (https://portals.broadinstitute.org/gppx/crispick/public) treating the consensus as a single-copy gene, conditions stated verbatim as Reference genome = Human GRCh38, Mechanism = CRISPRi, Enzyme = SpyoCas9; alternative Case 1 is manual 20 bp PAM-adjacent (NGG) design - no CRISPick tool/release version, no GRCh38 patch level, and candidate selection is stated only as 'based on scoring and minimum predicted off-target effect' with no numeric cutoff

Single-locus specificity check: run the candidate gRNA through the BLAT tool on the UCSC Genome Browser to confirm it targets only one genomic locus (alternative single-locus TE-targeting route) - the paper explicitly notes that stepSize, repMatch and minScore cannot be set in the web tool; no genome assembly stated for the web search, no UCSC/BLAT version, no hit-count or score acceptance criterion beyond 'only one single locus'

In-silico multi-locus target prediction with command-line BLAT (UCSC servers download), with a verbatim example command 'blat -stepSize=1 -repMatch=2000 -minScore=15 ./genome.fa ./guide1.fa ./guide1.blat.out' and prose rationale for each of the three parameters (small stepSize for sensitivity, repMatch >= subfamily size, lowered minScore for partial matches) - parameters are exact, but no BLAT version and no identity/build for './genome.fa' (no hg38/T2T declaration, no source, no checksum)

Annotation of BLAT hits by bedtools intersect (-a BLAT BED, -wo) against three -b annotation sets: RepeatMasker (subfamily/element identity), gene EXON coordinates (off-target calling, explicitly exons not genes), and gene intron coordinates (intragenic vs intergenic classification), with the verbatim example command 'bedtools intersect -a guide1.blat.bed -b gencode.gtf -wo > guide1.blat.intersect.gencode.out' - no bedtools version, no GENCODE release number, no RepeatMasker library version, and no described conversion of BLAT PSL output into the BED file the command consumes

Post-filtering of BLAT false positives (Troubleshooting Problem 1): discard hits matching fewer than 15-16 of the 20 gRNA bases, hits with more than 5-6 mismatches, and any hit with no PAM immediately downstream of the target site - thresholds are numeric but given as ranges ('15-16', '5-6') rather than a single value, no script, no tool and no PAM-scanning implementation is named

Unique-mapping bulk RNA-seq alignment of L1-CRISPRi vs non-targeting-control hiPSCs with STAR aligner (version 2.7.8a stated verbatim), one mapping locus only (--outFilterMultimapNmax 1) and mismatch-to-mapped-length ratio 0.03 (--outFilterMismatchNoverLmax), GENCODE annotation as guide GTF (--sjdbGTFfile); input libraries stranded, paired-end 2 x 150 bp - tool exactly pinned and the decisive options given verbatim, but the genome index is described only as 'the latest genome index' with no assembly, no patch and no GENCODE release

Strand-specific coverage and metaplot generation with deepTools (version 2.4.5 stated verbatim): bamCoverage to produce strand-specific bigwigs from the BAM/SAM alignments, then computeMatrix and plotHeatmap to build L1-subfamily heatmaps - tool exactly pinned, but not a single parameter is stated: no strand-selection flag, no bin size, no normalization method (CPM/RPKM/BPM/none), no computeMatrix mode/window/reference point, and no L1 region BED source

Quantitative sense/antisense split: alignment files split by strand using SAM flags with samtools view (version 1.16.1 stated verbatim), followed by generation of count matrices over the evolutionarily young full-length L1 elements to assess in-sense vs antisense transcription (featureCounts is cited in the reference list but never named in the step text) - tool exactly pinned and the operation is unambiguous, but the specific SAM flag combination is not enumerated, the counting tool is not named in the step, and the L1 element GTF/BED definition ('evolutionarily young, full-length, >6 kbp') has no stated coordinate source

Custom GTF construction to capture L1-ORF0-derived transcription: entries defined for regions 500 bp upstream of the L1 TSS in the opposite direction - the geometric definition is exact, but no script, no tool, no base annotation version and no handling rule for overlapping or truncated upstream regions is given

Peak calling on the dCas9, H3K4me3 and H3K9me3 CUT&RUN datasets with HOMER (version 5.1 stated verbatim), used to curate a list of targets displaying the expected CRISPRi effects (step is marked 'Optional') - tool exactly pinned, but no HOMER command is given: no makeTagDirectory settings, no findPeaks -style (factor/histone), no fragment length, no FDR or fold-vs-input threshold, and no statement of which sample serves as background/IgG control

Annotation of the called CUT&RUN peaks with bedtools intersect against RepeatMasker, exon and gene annotations to classify on-target L1 promoters vs off-target gene promoters - no bedtools version, no RepeatMasker library version, no GENCODE release, no overlap fraction or -wa/-wb/-wo mode stated for this instance, and no rule for how an overlap becomes an 'off-target' call
Baseline TE expression profiling in the chosen in-vitro model: hiPSC culture and pellet harvest for stranded paired-end 2 x 150 bp bulk RNA sequencing, minimum three technical replicates

Baseline H3K4me3 CUT&RUN epigenetic profiling of wild-type hiPSCs to identify active promoters of evolutionarily young L1s (Skene & Henikoff protocol; detailed protocol shared at dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.36wgqdb83vk5/v1)

ORF1p protein detection by western blot and/or immunocytochemistry (ORF1p green, DAPI nuclear counterstain) to confirm that expressed L1s produce protein; antibody specificity validation flagged as CRITICAL

Oligo ordering and gRNA cloning: 20 bp gRNA oligo pairs with BsmBI-compatible flanks (forward 5'-CACCG...3', reverse 5'-AAAC...C-3'), one gRNA per plasmid, cloned into the all-in-one dCas9-KRAB CRISPRi backbone RRID: Addgene_71237, plus a mandatory non-targeting control (lacZ or scrambled)
Third-generation lentiviral vector production (Zufferey et al. 1997) from the cloned plasmids and titration by qPCR of genomic DNA from serial-dilution transductions; titres no lower than 1e8 TU/ml

hiPSC culture on Lam521, Accutase passaging, lentiviral transduction at MOI 10 with 10 uM Rock inhibitor, day 7-10 establishment of the CRISPRi system, GFP+ FACS sorting of 100,000-200,000 cells, pelleting at 500 x g and snap-freezing for bulk RNA-seq plus replating for cryopreservation
H3K4me3 and H3K9me3 CUT&RUN epigenetic profiling of L1-CRISPRi hiPSCs and non-targeting control cells (native conditions; protocols.io DOI 10.17504/protocols.io.36wgqdb83vk5/v1)

dCas9 cross-linking CUT&RUN of L1-CRISPRi and control hiPSCs: 0.1% formaldehyde for 1 min (escalation to 1% if needed), wash buffers supplemented with 0.05% SDS and 1% Triton X-100, cross-link reversal with 0.09% SDS and 0.22 mg/ml proteinase K overnight at 55 C (protocols.io DOI 10.17504/protocols.io.bp2l6dr5rvqe/v1)

headline.static_readiness: 0/12 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 2/12 computational steps (C7 STAR 2.7.8a with --outFilterMultimapNmax 1 / --outFilterMismatchNoverLmax 0.03 stated verbatim, C9 samtools 1.16.1 strand splitting plus L1 count matrices). Both reach RI because the tool is exactly version-pinned, the deposited companion repository contains a named Snakemake pipeline for that stage, and at least one decisive parameter is stated. The remaining 10/12 steps cap at NI, and the blockers split into two distinct families. Family 1 (C1-C6, the gRNA design and in-silico target-prediction half of the protocol): every tool is unversioned (Dfam, CRISPick, BLAT, bedtools), no genome assembly is ever declared for the BLAT target ('./genome.fa'), no GENCODE or RepeatMasker release is named, and no executable artifact exists anywhere for these steps - the two example commands are prose, not code. Family 2 (C8, C10, C11, C12, the downstream profiling half): the tools ARE exactly pinned (deepTools 2.4.5, HOMER 5.1) but carry zero parameters - no bamCoverage bin size or normalization, no computeMatrix window, no HOMER findPeaks style/FDR/background, no bedtools overlap mode - so params=0 drives the axis minimum to zero. This is the paper's characteristic asymmetry: where a command is given it is exact (C4, C5, C7), and where a version is given it is exact (C7, C8, C9, C11), but the two almost never co-occur, and no step has both plus a pinned reference resource. Even at Stage 2, no step could exceed the environment closure that is actually deposited; capture_claim is 'release_snapshot' (two Zenodo-DOI-versioned code archives) rather than env_lock_claimed or container_digest_claimed, because neither the protocol text nor the repository README mentions a conda environment, a lockfile, a container image or an install procedure of any kind.
headline.coverage: 12 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML protocol text (Dfam consensus retrieval, CRISPick gRNA design, UCSC-BLAT single-locus check, command-line BLAT target prediction, bedtools annotation of BLAT hits, BLAT false-positive post-filtering, STAR unique mapping, deepTools strand-specific coverage/heatmaps, samtools strand splitting plus L1 count matrices, custom L1-ORF0 upstream GTF, HOMER CUT&RUN peak calling, bedtools annotation of CUT&RUN peaks). 8 wet-lab step groups counted in W but out of computational-reproduction scope: baseline bulk RNA-seq harvest, baseline H3K4me3 CUT&RUN, ORF1p western blot/immunocytochemistry, gRNA oligo cloning into Addgene_71237, third-generation lentiviral production and titration, hiPSC transduction and GFP+ FACS selection, native H3K4me3/H3K9me3 CUT&RUN on CRISPRi lines, and cross-linked dCas9 CUT&RUN. Computational coverage = 12/20 = 60%.

gaps.where: All 12 computational steps - reference genome, annotation and repeat-library versions
gaps.missing: Not one reference resource is versioned anywhere in the protocol. The BLAT command consumes './genome.fa' with no assembly named; the bedtools example consumes 'gencode.gtf' with no GENCODE release; the STAR step says only 'the latest genome index and GENCODE annotation as guide GTF', which is a moving target by construction; RepeatMasker is invoked three times (C5, C12) with no library version; Dfam is used for the consensus with no release and no family accession (DF number); CRISPick is configured with 'Human GRCh38 (or the more recent annotation T2T ... if it is implemented)' with no patch level and no decision recorded. Because the whole point of the protocol is locus-specific TE analysis, an annotation-release change silently changes which L1 loci exist in the count matrix.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact assembly (e.g. GRCh38.p14 with the download URL and checksum), the GENCODE release number, the RepeatMasker library version, and the Dfam release plus the DF accessions of L1HS and L1PA2; replace 'the latest genome index' with the pinned index actually used.

gaps.where: C1-C6 - unversioned software in the gRNA design and target-prediction half
gaps.missing: Dfam (web resource), CRISPick (web tool), BLAT (both the UCSC web tool and the command-line binary downloaded from the UCSC servers) and bedtools all appear with no version number. BLAT in particular is scored differently across releases, and the protocol's central recommendation is to lower minScore below the default - a threshold whose meaning is only interpretable against a known BLAT version. The four exactly pinned tools (STAR 2.7.8a, deepTools 2.4.5, samtools 1.16.1, HOMER 5.1) all sit in the downstream half, so the pinning is partial across the pipeline.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a version to every named tool including the web tools (CRISPick release date, UCSC BLAT/blat binary version, bedtools version) and ship them together in a conda environment file or container so the whole protocol has one environment rather than four pinned tools inside an unpinned pipeline.

gaps.where: C8, C11, C12 - named-and-versioned tools invoked with no parameters at all
gaps.missing: deepTools 2.4.5 bamCoverage/computeMatrix/plotHeatmap (C8) is described only by function name: no strand-selection flag, no --binSize, no normalization (CPM/RPKM/BPM/None), no --extendReads, no computeMatrix mode (scale-regions vs reference-point), no window and no L1 region BED. HOMER 5.1 (C11) has no makeTagDirectory settings, no findPeaks -style, no fragment length, no FDR or fold-over-background cutoff, and no statement of which library serves as the background/IgG control. The C12 bedtools annotation has no overlap mode or minimum overlap fraction and no rule converting an overlap into an 'off-target' call. In each case the parameter set, not the tool, determines the result.
gaps.how_to_close: Print the exact command line for each of these three steps in the protocol text (the paper already does this well for BLAT and bedtools in C4/C5), including the region BED file used for the L1 heatmaps and the background sample used for peak calling.

gaps.where: C1-C6 - no executable artifact for the gRNA design / in-silico off-target half of the protocol
gaps.missing: The linked repository (Molecular-Neurogenetics/L1CRISPR_Adami_2025) covers the bulk RNA-seq and CUT&RUN processing pipelines and the 10X/trusTEr analyses; its README lists no script for consensus retrieval, gRNA design, BLAT target prediction, PSL-to-BED conversion, or the false-positive post-filter. Those steps exist only as two example command lines and a prose threshold list ('fewer than 15-16 bases', 'more than 5-6 bases mismatch'), which is exactly the half of the protocol the paper presents as its novel contribution.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the gRNA design and BLAT off-target analysis as a small runnable workflow (input: subfamily consensus FASTA; output: annotated candidate-target BED with the false-positive filter applied) and deposit it with a DOI alongside the existing pipelines.

gaps.where: Whole protocol - provenance of code and data is delegated to the companion research article
gaps.missing: The availability statement reads verbatim 'No original data or code was generated in this publication. All the data or code presented in this work have been published in the original research paper Adami et al., 2025.' Nothing in the protocol maps its numbered steps onto specific files in the two cited repositories, so a reader following the protocol cannot tell which deposited script implements which step; the mapping used in this assessment (C7-C12 -> Snakefile_bulkRNAseq / Snakefile_cutnrun) was inferred from the repository README, not stated by the paper. The repository README additionally carries a naming-inconsistency warning in its own prose ('the gRNAs in the bulk datasets are named differently in the samplesheet and scripts! ... gRNA3 in the sample names and samplesheet is gRNA1 in the manuscript'), which is a live mismatch between deposited artifact and publication.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a step-to-script table in the protocol mapping each numbered step to the file path and DOI version of the deposited implementation, and reconcile the gRNA naming between samplesheets, scripts and manuscript in a tagged release.

gaps.where: C6 - false-positive filter thresholds given as ranges
gaps.missing: The filter is specified as 'fewer than 15-16 bases' matched and 'more than 5-6 bases' mismatched out of 20. Two readers applying 15 versus 16, or 5 versus 6, obtain different target sets, and the protocol gives no rule for choosing. The PAM-absence exclusion has no implementation (no PAM-scanning tool or window is named).
gaps.how_to_close: State the single threshold actually used in the case study, and provide the PAM check as a script rather than a criterion.

gaps.where: C1, C2, C3 - web-resource dependence with no snapshot
gaps.missing: Three steps depend on live web services whose state is not archived: the Dfam consensus download, the CRISPick design run, and the UCSC Genome Browser BLAT search. None of the retrieved outputs (the consensus FASTA, the CRISPick .txt result table, the UCSC BLAT hit list) is deposited as a supplementary file, so the actual inputs to the case study's gRNA selection cannot be recovered even though the final gRNA sequences are given in the Key Resource Table.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the exact consensus FASTA, the CRISPick output table and the BLAT hit tables used in the case study as supplementary files or in the Zenodo record, with retrieval dates.

gaps.where: Data availability - sequencing data are public but the protocol's own case-study linkage is indirect
gaps.missing: The sequencing data are deposited and public (GEO GSE283600, released 16 Jun 2025, 83 samples across NextSeq 500 / NovaSeq 6000 / PromethION), which is why every step scores data=2. However the protocol does not state which GSM samples correspond to which protocol step, and the deposited Zenodo image record (10.5281/zenodo.17314543) and Key-Resource-Table record (10.5281/zenodo.17435054) are cited by DOI only, with no description of contents in the paper text.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a short table mapping protocol steps to GSM/GSE sub-series accessions, and describe the contents of each Zenodo deposit in the availability statement.

gaps.missing: hiPSC culture and RNA-seq harvest, baseline H3K4me3 CUT&RUN, ORF1p western blot/immunocytochemistry, gRNA cloning into Addgene_71237, third-generation lentiviral production and qPCR titration, MOI-10 transduction and GFP+ FACS selection, native H3K4me3/H3K9me3 CUT&RUN, and cross-linked dCas9 CUT&RUN are physical steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W, not verdicted. Note that the wet-lab half is unusually well specified for a preprint (two protocols.io DOIs, Addgene RRID, explicit MOI, cell numbers, formaldehyde concentrations and incubation times), so the reproducibility asymmetry in this paper runs opposite to the usual direction: bench detail exceeds computational detail.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness. The bench half already meets a high standard; bringing the in-silico half (C1-C6) up to the same level of explicitness would be the highest-leverage change.
